Article Title: Kick streamer Clavicular says Kick spent nearly $700K promoting his clips and gives creators an unlimited clipping budget
Article Text:
Image/Instagram

Clavicular reveals Kick spent $700K on viral clip promotions and creator growth

“no clipping spend”

“unlimited.”

Kick streamer Clavicular credits viral growth to looksmaxxing content

Kick streamer Clavicular has revealed that he does not spend money on promoting his viral short clips because Kick pays for the campaigns. The streamer claimed that Kick has spent close to $700,000 in one month to promote his clips across platforms like TikTok and YouTube Shorts. He explained that the goal is to bring more viewers to Kick through branded clips. Clavicular shared these details during an appearance on the Iced Coffee Hour podcast.During the podcast, Clavicular was asked how he manages to get billions of views from short videos without spending money himself. He said he hasbecause Kick handles the cost of promoting his content.According to Clavicular, Kick pays for the clips because they include a large kick.com/clavvicular logo. He explained that the platform benefits because viewers who watch the clips may visit Kick and become new users.The streamer said this system is not only for him but is available to other creators on Kick as well. When asked about the size of his clipping budget, Clavicular described it asHe explained that the amount Kick spends can change depending on advertising prices. According to him, Kick adjusts its spending based on CPM, which means the cost of reaching a certain number of viewers.Clavicular also claimed that Kick’s investment in his clips reached almost $700,000 during one month. He said the strategy helped his content reach a huge audience, with his clips reportedly gaining around 2.2 billion views in a month.Clavicular believes his fast growth comes from a mix of factors, including the popularity of his looksmaxxing-related content and viewers’ interest in watching his daily life.He described the growth as a new type of online trend where audiences become interested in following a creator’s lifestyle, opinions, and personal journey.The streamer’s comments highlight how platforms are increasingly investing in creator promotion to attract more users. Instead of creators paying for advertisements themselves, platforms like Kick can use branded clips as a way to promote both the streamer and their own service.However, Clavicular’s claims about Kick’s spending have not been independently confirmed by the platform. His comments provide his view of how the promotion system works and how it has helped increase his online reach.As short-form videos continue to play a major role in creator growth, platforms are looking for new ways to turn viral moments into long-term audiences. Clavicular says Kick’s support has played a major role in helping his content reach millions of viewers worldwide.
Article Summary: Kick streamer Clavicular has revealed that he does not spend money on promoting his viral short clips because Kick pays for the campaigns. The streamer claimed that Kick spent close to $700,000 in one month to promote his clips across platforms like TikTok and YouTube Shorts.

Article Title: Why did Joe accuse Twitch streamer Yugi of ‘lying’ about his Valorant rank? Viral clip explained
Article Text:
Why did Joe accuse Twitch streamer Yugi of ‘lying’ about his Valorant rank? Viral clip explained (Image via Getty)

Joe accuses Twitch streamer Yugi of lying about his Valorant rank

Reddit users bring up earlier claims involving Yugi

Twitch streamer Yugi is facing criticism after a clip from a recent 1v1 gaming bet with fellow streamer Joe sparked debate online. The clip was shared on the r/LivestreamFail subreddit by a Reddit user. In the video, Joe accused Yugi of lying about his Valorant rank before their match. According to Joe, Yugi had told him he had only reached Silver rank, even though he had allegedly peaked at Immortal. The exchange quickly became one of the main talking points in the livestream community, with Reddit users adding more context and sharing similar allegations.The argument happened after the Valorant 1v1 match. Joe admitted that he had lost but said his frustration was not about the result. Instead, he claimed Yugi had not been honest about his previous rank before the wager.Joe said:"Sure. I lost. But stop with this ****** hustle-*** bullshit. You’re saying you peaked Immortal, bro, and you lied, and you said you peaked Silver. You did. You lied."Yugi denied the accusation during the exchange. Joe continued to insist that Yugi had described himself as a Silver player before the match.He added:"You said you peaked Silver. You ****** said you peaked Silver.You said that flat out. No no no. ****** liar."The clip was later posted on r/LivestreamFail , where viewers discussed what happened and why Joe reacted so strongly.One Reddit user, Demacian_Justice, explained that the Valorant match was only part of a larger wager between the two streamers. Earlier, they had also played GeoGuessr. Since Joe believed he had a clear advantage in that game, he chose to play with a handicap to make the contest more balanced.The Reddit user wrote:"A huge part of why Joe is so pissed here, besides just being Joe, is that when they had played GeoGuessr 1v1s earlier in the bet, Joe played with a major handicap to make it fair since he was significantly better at the game.”According to the Reddit comment, Joe felt frustrated because he believed he had adjusted the earlier match to keep things fair, while Yugi had not been equally honest before the Valorant game.The discussion did not stop with the viral clip. Several Reddit users claimed they had seen similar situations involving Yugi before, although these claims have not been independently verified.Reddit user MesocosmFather commented:"Swear, Yugi has done this multiple times before. Is his content just rage bait and lying?"Another Reddit user, imSidroc, also referred to a previous Valorant event.They wrote:"Yugi also lied about his rank in that 2v2 Valorant tournament recently. Really ***** cringe behavior. Should be treated like stealing money from these companies and streamers because that's what he's essentially doing."These comments reflect opinions shared by Reddit users and remain unverified. At the time of writing, neither Yugi nor Joe had publicly responded to the wider Reddit discussion beyond what was shown in the livestream clip.The clip continues to draw attention as viewers debate whether Joe's accusations were justified and whether Yugi had actually misrepresented his skill level before the wager.
Article Summary: Joe accuses Twitch streamer Yugi of lying about his Valorant rank before 1v1 match. Joe claims Yugi told him he had only reached Silver rank, even though he had allegedly peaked at Immortal. Viewers debate whether Joe's accusations were justified and whether Yugi had actually misrepresented his skill level before the wager.

Article Title: YouTuber Hank Green faces backlash after admitting AI use in research for Ask Hank Anything episode
Article Text:
Getty Images

Hank Green responds after AI research admission sparks criticism

"bad habit"

Hank Green apologizes after AI research use sparks trust concerns among fans



"mortified"

YouTuber and science educator Hank Green is facing criticism after admitting he used AI to help research a recent episode of his Ask Hank Anything series. The debate started after viewers shared a clip from the episode online and claimed one part sounded like it came from an AI chatbot. Green denied that AI wrote the line but admitted he had used ChatGPT during his research. He later apologized, saying he had relied too much on AI while working under heavy pressure.The controversy began after an episode of Ask Hank Anything featuring creator Soupytime was uploaded to the Complexly YouTube channel on July 30. Soon after, a clip from the video spread across social media. Many viewers believed one of Green's comments sounded like an AI-generated response.Green later checked his script and research notes. He said the line in question was not written by ChatGPT. According to him, it was something he said on the spot while talking about a disagreement with Soupytime.However, Green admitted that he had used ChatGPT to help with research for the episode. He explained that he had been depending too much on AI-generated notes because he was very busy and under a lot of pressure while making videos.He called it aand accepted that it was the wrong choice. Green also made it clear that AI did not write his script and that he still formed his own opinions after reading and learning from different sources.Even after Green explained what happened, many viewers remained unhappy. Some said they were disappointed because Green is known for making educational videos that people trust. Others worried that AI can sometimes give incorrect information, making it harder to know what parts of the episode were fully checked.Some viewers also noticed several fact-checking notes in the episode that questioned claims about topics such as cat saliva, mantis shrimp vision, and artificial sweeteners. This led to even more discussion about how the research was done.Later, Green posted a long apology. He said he wasthat he had let viewers down and promised to change how he works. He explained that he mainly used AI to help find research papers and other resources, not to create his opinions or write his final message.Green also admitted that using AI and trying to make too much content had become unhealthy. He said his wife Katherine and his brother John had both raised concerns. Because of this, Green announced that viewers should expect fewer videos for now. He said projects like SMUSH and 4×3 are being paused, and Hankschannel may also take a break while he focuses on a long-term project.The incident has started a bigger discussion about how AI should be used in educational content. While Green has apologized and promised to make changes, many viewers say trust is the most important part of science communication and hope he will rebuild it through his future work.
Article Summary: Hank Green apologizes after AI research use sparks trust concerns among fans. Viewers shared a clip from the episode online and claimed one part sounded like it came from an AI chatbot. Green denied that AI wrote the line but admitted he had used ChatGPT. He later apologized, saying he had relied too much on AI while working under heavy pressure.

Article Title: Why is Kick streamer JollyRancherZoo facing ‘backlash’? Viral India horse riding clip explained
Article Text:
Why is Kick streamer JollyRancherZoo facing ‘backlash’? Viral India horse riding clip explained (Image via Getty)



JollyRancherZoo Heard Asking the Horse to Go Faster in Viral Clip

JollyRancherZoo Seems to React to the Flak

Kick streamer JollyRancherZoo is facing criticism online after a clip from her India trip showed her riding a horse that viewers described as extremely thin and unwell. The video was shared on Reddit on July 29 and quickly drew strong reactions from people who watched it. In the clip, JollyRancherZoo is seen riding the horse while her cameraman follows her. She can be heard asking for the horse to go faster. Viewers questioned why she was riding the animal and said it appeared to be struggling as it moved.The clip shows JollyRancherZoo sitting on the horse as she travels with her cameraman. During the ride, she appears to want the horse to pick up speed."I'm tryna go fast, man... I think he's gonna go super fast. Sorry, run? It's gonna run, maybe?"She is also heard repeatedly asking the handler to go faster.The horse's condition became the main focus of the backlash. Several viewers pointed to its visible ribs and bones and said the animal looked too weak to carry a rider. One Reddit user wrote that the horse was "skin and bones" and called the situation sad. Another said seeing the animal was upsetting and wrote that it was "not cool at all."A third user questioned whether the horse was having trouble walking on its back legs.These comments were viewers' personal observations and were not supported by a veterinary assessment in the discussion.Furthermore, there were other complaints against JollyRancherZoo from people who thought that the girl would have realized the state of the horse before getting onto it. There were those who blamed the horse owners more for using the horse in that way.As the backlash continued on the internet, it seems like JollyRancherZoo reacted by reposting a piece of content from the X platform to give more information regarding the situation. As per the information in the post, it is clear that the video did not capture everything else that happened in the livestream.The post claimed that JollyRancherZoo did not actually want the horse to run and that she felt bad after becoming aware of its condition. However, the available Reddit discussion does not independently confirm those claims, so they remain part of the response surrounding the controversy rather than facts.The incident has now become another example of how quickly livestream moments can spread beyond their original audience. The clip could be watched independently of the entire streaming and the sequence that preceded and followed the clip. In this situation, the audience paid attention to the visuals in the clip and questioned whether it was right to ride the horse.The debate is still centered around the social media population. The main point raised is about the state of the horse and the act of riding it. JollyRancherZoo's reported response has added another part to the story, but the full context of what happened during the livestream is still being debated online.
Article Summary: Kick streamer JollyRancherZoo is facing criticism online after a clip from her India trip showed her riding a horse that viewers described as extremely thin and unwell. The video was shared on Reddit on July 29 and quickly drew strong reactions from people who watched it. Viewers questioned why she was riding the animal and said it appeared to be struggling.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Daisaku Ikeda: 'A peaceful life does not mean a life free of toil and suffering' and the true meaning of happiness
Article Text:
Happiness quote of the day by Daisaku Ikeda.

What does the quote mean?

Peace that lives inside you

Who was Daisaku Ikeda?

Famous Japanese Buddhist philosopher Daisaku Ikeda, who is known for turning Soka Gakkai into a massive international organization, made a happy and peaceful life look simple. He said a peaceful life does not mean a life free of toil and suffering; rather, it means living without being swayed no matter what happens. This is a state of true peace and happiness.True peace is not a passive state where everything goes smoothly, but it is an active inner strength that stays calm through challenges. This stands opposite to what people generally believe.Most people define peace as the absence of trouble. They believe they will finally be peaceful when their work stress ends, their health problems resolve, or their financial worries disappear. This quote turns that common idea upside down. It asserts that waiting for a life completely free of effort and suffering is a trap, because life by its very nature brings unexpected obstacles, hard work, and emotional pain. If your peace depends on everything outside of you being perfectly calm, you will spend your whole life at the mercy of shifting circumstances.True peace is the ability to remain balanced, grounded, and clear-headed regardless of what happens around you.It is about building an unshakable mindset. When severe weather hits, a shallow tree gets pulled out of the soil by its roots, but a deeply rooted tree sways with the wind without breaking. Living without being swayed means you develop roots deep enough to withstand emotional and situational storms. You still feel the pain, and you still do the hard work required to handle your life, but those difficulties do not destroy your inner composure or rob you of your purpose.The quote also redefines happiness. Many people confuse short-term pleasure with real happiness. Pleasure depends on external triggers like praise, comfort, or success. When those triggers vanish, the pleasure disappears with them, often leaving behind fear or disappointment. Real happiness, as described in the quote, is closely tied to resilience. It comes from knowing that your sense of self and your emotional stability do not depend on external validation or smooth sailing. It is the steady confidence that comes from facing difficulties without losing your center.Daisaku Ikeda (1928–2023) was an influential Japanese Buddhist philosopher, educator, author, and peacebuilder. Best known as the founding president of Soka Gakkai International, he transformed a localized Japanese lay movement into one of the world's largest community-based Buddhist organizations, spanning around 190 countries and territories.Born in Tokyo to a family of seaweed farmers, Ikeda’s youth was heavily shaped by the devastation of World War II. The conflict inspired a lifelong dedication to rooting out human suffering and fostering global peace. In 1947, he met Josei Toda, the second president of Soka Gakkai, who became his mentor. Following Toda’s death, Ikeda assumed the presidency in 1960 at age 32. Under his leadership, the organization expanded beyond religious practice to engage deeply in educational, cultural, and human rights initiatives worldwide.At the core of Ikeda’s philosophy was the concept of "human revolution", the idea that a self-directed, positive transformation within an individual can ultimately lead to positive change in society. He championed dialogue as the primary tool for overcoming cultural, political, and ideological divisions. Beginning in the 1970s, he engaged in published conversations with world figures, scholars, and leaders, including British historian Arnold J. Toynbee and former Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.
Article Summary: Daisaku Ikeda was an influential Japanese Buddhist philosopher, educator, author, and peacebuilder. Best known as the founding president of Soka Gakkai International, he transformed a localized Japanese lay movement into one of the world's largest community-based Buddhist organizations.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Masashi Kishimoto: 'The difference between insanity and genius is measured only by success and failure' and the brutal bias that turns madmen into visionaries
Article Text:
Masashi Kishimoto is a Japanese manga artist best known for creating the globally acclaimed manga and anime series Naruto

Kishimoto's difficult road to success

Why success changes how we judge ideas

Why the quote still matters today

In 1997, a young Japanese artist spent long nights in a small studio working on a story about a lonely boy who carried a powerful monster inside him. At the time, the idea went against what most manga publishers wanted. Main characters were expected to be easy to like, not social outcasts with painful pasts. Some people believed the story was too dark to succeed in a popular magazine.That artist was Masashi Kishimoto. Two years later, Naruto began serialization in Weekly Shōnen Jump and went on to sell more than 250 million copies worldwide. Looking back on the fine line between failure and success, Kishimoto summed it up with a simple observation:"The difference between insanity and genius is measured only by success and failure."His words point to the way society judges people who take risks. When someone pursues an unusual idea and fails, they are often called reckless, unrealistic, or even crazy. But if that same idea succeeds, people suddenly describe the creator as a genius or visionary. Kishimoto's quote reminds us that public opinion often depends more on the final result than on the idea itself.Masashi Kishimoto was born in Okayama Prefecture in 1974. As a child, he loved manga and anime, especially Doraemon and Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball.But becoming a professional manga artist was far from easy.After winning Shueisha's Hop Step Award in 1995 for his one-shot manga Karakuri, Kishimoto spent several years submitting new ideas to editors. Many were rejected before he finally found success with Naruto.At the time, the manga industry was highly competitive. Weekly Shōnen Jump relied on weekly reader surveys, and series that ranked poorly for several weeks could be cancelled almost immediately.Even then, Kishimoto refused to simplify his story. He wanted characters with tragic pasts, morally complex villains, and storylines that developed slowly over time instead of following simple good-versus-evil formulas. If Naruto had failed early on, many people would likely have called his approach unrealistic. Because it became a huge success, those same creative choices are now seen as one of the series' greatest strengths.Although similar ideas have been expressed by writers such as Alexandre Dumas and Lord Byron, Kishimoto's version reflects his own experience working in Japan's highly competitive manga industry.Kishimoto's quote reflects a well-known concept in psychology called outcome bias. This is the tendency to judge a decision based mainly on how it turns out rather than whether it was a reasonable decision at the time.A similar idea appears in the philosophy of William James, one of the founders of pragmatism. In Pragmatism (1907), James argued that people often judge ideas by their practical results rather than by their original value.History offers many examples. Thomas Edison tested thousands of materials while trying to invent a practical light bulb. Before he succeeded, many people viewed his repeated failures as stubbornness. After his invention worked, those same efforts became a symbol of determination.The opposite also happens. Many inventors and creators who took similar risks but failed are largely forgotten today, even if their ideas were just as bold.In reality, the daily lives of a genius and someone whose ideas fail can look very similar. Both may spend years working alone, ignoring criticism, and focusing completely on a goal. Society usually decides whether to call them brilliant or foolish only after the outcome is known.Kishimoto's observation remains relevant in today's world, especially in industries such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and space technology.Many startup founders with unusual ideas are dismissed at first because their plans seem unrealistic. Yet when those ideas succeed, the same people are praised for thinking differently.A well-known example is SpaceX. In its early years, many experts doubted that reusable rockets could land vertically after launch. Once the company repeatedly proved it could be done, the idea quickly became accepted across the space industry.Psychologist and Nobel Prize-winning economist Daniel Kahneman also explored this pattern in Thinking, Fast and Slow. He explained that people often praise bold decisions when they lead to success but criticize the very same decisions when they end in failure.Understanding this bias can help people judge ideas more fairly. Instead of relying only on results, it is often more useful to ask whether an idea was well thought out, carefully planned, and based on sound reasoning.Before Naruto became one of the world's best-selling manga series, Kishimoto spent years dealing with rejection, failed ideas, and long hours of work with little recognition. His quote is a reminder that many creative ideas are judged only after they succeed, not while they are still taking shape.
Article Summary: Masashi Kishimoto is a Japanese manga artist best known for creating the globally acclaimed manga and anime series Naruto. His words point to the way society judges people who take risks. When someone pursues an unusual idea and fails, they are often called reckless, unrealistic, or even crazy. If that same idea succeeds, people suddenly describe the creator as a genius or visionary.

Article Title: Broad Peak avalanche: Three of 10 missing climbers found dead in PoK
Article Text:
Broad Peak avalanche leaves three dead

Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on PoK's Broad Peak recovered three bodies on Friday after locating four victims, as harsh weather and poor flying conditions hampered helicopter search-and-rescue operations.The Gilgit-Baltistan regional government identified the three recovered bodies as Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, Omani climber Nathira Ahmed, and American climber Mallory Geis. Authorities said the bodies were transported to a hospital for further procedures, as cited by AP.Adverse weather continued to hamper rescue operations on Friday, with poor flying conditions limiting search efforts, Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister Amjad Hussain said in a statement.The announcement came hours after officials said search teams had located the bodies of four climbers, though the identity of the fourth victim has not yet been confirmed. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to brief the media.According to Karrar Haidri, vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, the climbers lost contact with their base camp after an avalanche struck Broad Peak while they were attempting to scale the mountain.“The team has been out of communication since Thursday,” said Haidri, adding that Pakistan Army helicopters were assisting in the search-and-rescue operation.The expedition included five Nepali climbers, along with climbers from Oman, the United States, Pakistan, China, and another foreign national. The Pakistani climber was identified as Sohail Sakhi, while the Chinese climber was identified only by the surname Wang.China said it was working to verify whether any of its nationals were among the 10 climbers reported missing.The expedition was led by renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja , a Nepal-born former British Army soldier widely known as Nims Dai. Purja gained global recognition after climbing the world's 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, a feat documented in the Netflix film 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible. His record was later surpassed in 2023.Pakistan-based adventure company Moving Mountains said last month that the team had begun its journey to the town of Askole before attempting to summit Broad Peak, wishing the climbers a safe expedition.According to the company's website, the climb marked Mallory Geis' first attempt at an 8,000-metre peak in Pakistan. For Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, a guide with the company, as well as a geographer and high-altitude photographer who had scaled several of the world's highest mountains, it was expected to be his final expedition to an 8,000-metre peak.Geis, 39, who lived in San Antonio, had announced on social media earlier this year that she was closing her Pilates studio to pursue mountaineering full time, writing that she was taking “a giant leap of faith into the unknown to see where life goes. I have a sneaking suspicion there will be lots of helmets, harnesses, and crampons involved.”At 8,047 metres (26,401 feet), Broad Peak is the world's 12th-highest mountain. It is located in PoK's Karakoram range, which is home to five of the world's 14 peaks above 8,000 metres and attracts mountaineers from across the globe.Mountaineering accidents are not uncommon in northern Pakistan, where climbers frequently contend with avalanches, harsh terrain and rapidly changing weather conditions.
Article Summary: Search teams have recovered the bodies of three of the 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak. The bodies have been identified as Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, Omani climber Nathira Ahmed, and American climber Mallory Geis. The identity of the fourth victim has not been confirmed.

Article Title: 'Flawed' Reflecting Pool renovation: US drops vandalism charges against former Olympian David Hearn
Article Text:
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is seen from the Washington Monument, Friday, July 31, 2026, in Washington. (Photo: AP)

The US justice department recently admitted the “hasty and botched” nature of President Donald Trump’s $14.7 million renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, dropping criminal charges of vandalism against former Olympian David Hearn.Earlier, Trump, along with DC US Attorney Jeanine Pirro, had publicly accused Hearn, along with three others, of damaging the pool lining, algae blooms and green-hued water in the pool. According to DC court records, charges were dropped against at least one of those people as well on Friday.Trump had ordered renovations to the 600-metre pool in May, to be completed by the US Independence Day- July four. His renovation efforts drew significant criticism owing to their price and changes that included painting the bottom with "American flag blue".On June 11, a National Park Service engineer alerted the Interior Department of the peeling, which the prosecutors noted, on Friday, was the same part of the pool liner Hearn was accused of ripping up. Hearn was arrested eight days later and then indicted on July two.On Friday, Hearn's lawyers said that he "did nothing wrong". The former Olympic canoeist pleaded not guilty this month, while acknowledging he reached into the pool while cycling and touched a piece of pool liner, already detached partially.According to CNN, the peeling away of the blue linings from the bottom of the pool came more than a week before Hearn visited the landmark.“The damage was the result of a botched installation and not vandalism as initially represented by the Department of the Interior (DOI). Indeed, USAO-DC could only rely on the information provided by DOI that the damage was entirely caused by vandals”, Pirro’s office wrote on Friday, accusing several federal agencies, including DOI.“It was not until after the return of the indictment [of Hearn] that the [Department of Interior] provided additional documents to the [US Attorney’s Office in DC] indicating that damage to the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in June 2026 was the result of flawed installation by the contractor, Atlantic Industrial Coatings”, it added.As per prosecutors, the work was rushed because of the events being hosted on the National Mall for the celebration of the 250th year of American independence.
Article Summary: Former Olympian David Hearn was accused of damaging the pool lining, algae blooms and green-hued water in the pool. Trump had ordered renovations to the 600-metre pool in May, to be completed by the US Independence Day- July four. On Friday, Hearn's lawyers said that he "did nothing wrong"

Article Title: Trump threatens to hit Iran 'very hard' as US weighs fresh attack
Article Text: US President Donald Trump on Friday threatened to hit Iran "very hard", as reports suggested his administration was weighing a fresh wave of strikes as early as this weekend, potentially targeting the country's energy infrastructure.The threat comes after more than five months of conflict, which began on February 28 when the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran. Since then, both sides have continued exchanging attacks."We'll be hitting him very hard and, you know, at some point they're going to say, 'We just can't take it anymore,'" Trump said during a cabinet meeting at the Camp David presidential retreat in Maryland.According to The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed US officials, Trump has ordered preparations for a new military campaign aimed at pressuring Tehran to surrender, with operations possibly beginning this weekend.Separately, CBS News reported that the United States and Israel are discussing coordinated strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, including oil refineries and power plants, that could be carried out over the weekend.Trump has repeatedly warned that Iran's critical infrastructure could be targeted. Last week, he said the United States would destroy a bridge or power plant every time ships were attacked in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.While CBS reported that Trump had not yet given final approval for the operation, it said Washington and Israel were closely coordinating the plans. The report came days after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met Trump and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington.The report also said some White House aides raised strong objections to the proposal during the cabinet meeting.If approved, the operation would mark the first time Israel has directly joined a new phase of strikes on Iran since the opening weeks of the war.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "very hard" Reports suggest his administration was weighing a fresh wave of strikes as early as this weekend, potentially targeting the country's energy infrastructure. The threat comes after more than five months of conflict, which began in February.

Article Title: 'I'm still in shock my OPT is revoked': Indian student's appeal to choose 'legit employers' in US goes viral; 'Asked me to leave in 30 days'
Article Text:
Indian student's warning to fellow students after STEM OPT visa gets revoked (Photo: AI)

OPT fraud cases in the US

An Indian student's appeal that fellow Indians should not fall for bogus companies in the US has now gone viral as the student shared the experience of getting STEM OPT revoked because the company did not have any US presence. The student shared the experience anonymously in a job group for OPT and CPT students. The screenshot has gone viral for many reasons."Today I'm crying because my STEM OPT has been cancelled after they issued me the EAD card because the company I'm with are based in India and they only have mailing box on the address and none of them reside in the US. USCIS audited them and they didn't find any office or employer locally in the US and they sent me EAD revocation letter and asked me to leave in 30 days," the post said."My journey in the US is over, but I urge all of you to immediately move to employers who are legit and who are present in person in the US and who have a physical desk where he sits in the US," the message read."The consultancy earlier mentioned they have an office but they only had a mailing address and they were minting crores of rupees while jeopardizing the careers of US students. They didn't lose anything but as a student I lost my American Dream," it added."I never thought my journey would end like this...my life has ended here but I want to save all of you. I'm still in shock my OPT is revoked," the post said.In May, Immigration and Customs Enforcement identified over 10,000 cases of OPT fraud. OPT allows foreign students to work in the US for 12 months, and STEM OPT for 24 months. ICE and USCIS officials jointly announced how they conducted site visits and found out that several of these OPT beneficiaries were being managed from India.
Article Summary: An Indian student's appeal that fellow Indians should not fall for bogus companies in the US has now gone viral. The student shared the experience of getting STEM OPT revoked because the company did not have any US presence. In May, Immigration and Customs Enforcement identified over 10,000 cases of OPT fraud.

Article Title: 'Not agreed to that': Trump shifts stance on Ukraine building Patriot missiles
Article Text:
Trump changes stance on letting Ukraine build Patriot

US President Donald Trump said Friday that Washington has not agreed to Ukraine producing Patriot surface-to-air interceptor missiles, walking back earlier signals that Kyiv would be granted a production licence."We have not agreed to that," Trump said, adding that the US has "to be very careful about letting somebody build them."Trump's remarks mark a shift from his earlier comments at the Nato summit in Turkey, where he had signalled Washington would grant Kyiv a licence to produce the missiles. Following a White House meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday, Zelenskyy had said Trump "accepted that he will give us licences."Trump told the Financial Times on Thursday that he was "not sure" whether Washington would grant the licence, adding that "we're looking at it." His latest comments appear to further distance the US from committing to the production deal.The Patriot system is vital for Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian ballistic missiles targeting Kyiv and other cities. Lockheed Martin and RTX jointly produce the interceptors.Persuading Trump to allow Kyiv to produce the missiles has been a significant diplomatic objective for Zelenskyy.Trump also confirmed that his two envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, will visit Ukraine for the first time in the coming days. The president said his focus remains on ending the war. "Very simply put, we want the war in Ukraine with Russia ended. I'm not looking for missiles. We're looking for peace."In the same interview with the FT, Trump addressed the Middle East, insisting that Iran would eventually submit despite its recent strikes across the region. "We are beating the hell out of them," he said.The US president also expressed optimism about finalising the landmark civil nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia unveiled last week. Trump said he has spoken to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about normalising ties, adding "it could happen."Trump also complimented UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham for signalling a pragmatic approach on North Sea oil exploration. "The one thing that seems to be loud and clear is that he wants to make his country rich, and he knows that he can do that by opening up the North Sea oil," Trump said of their first call last week.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump says Washington has not agreed to Ukraine producing Patriot surface-to-air interceptor missiles. Trump's remarks mark a shift from his earlier comments at the Nato summit in Turkey, where he had signalled Washington would grant Kyiv a licence. The Patriot system is vital for Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian ballistic missiles.
